overall: Atlanta is experiencing a post-frontal pattern on June 23, with mostly sunny skies and northwest winds 10–15 mph gusting to 25 mph. This northwest flow is bringing notably below-average temperatures for late June in Atlanta, where mid-90s would be more typical, with today's high forecast only near 83°F. The active flood warnings are for the Satilla River in far South Georgia (Pierce, Ware, and Brantley Counties) and have no bearing on Atlanta's temperature forecast.
forecast_obs_notes: No intraday observations or NWP model TMAX grids are available yet (before 7am ET), so the analysis relies entirely on the official NWS text forecast. max_temp_prediction: With mostly sunny skies and a persistent northwest wind, the main uncertainty is whether the gusty flow suppresses the afternoon high slightly below the 83°F NWS target or whether peak solar heating nudges it a degree or two higher. The northwest wind component acts as a mild cap on mixing and limits boundary-layer deepening, making a landing right around 83°F most likely. Confidence is moderate-high given strong NWS signal and no convective interference, with the realistic range being roughly 81–85°F.
